conventions.convention: The second variation is the second derivative itself, without a factor of one half. Curves and fixed-endpoint variations are restrictions of C² maps on open intervals; the action uses a C² Lagrangian on an open chart containing [a,b] × U × Rⁿ.

Oscillator extrema are assessed among fixed-endpoint curves using the supremum distance of the sum of absolute differences of the curve and its first two derivatives. The sign-changing conclusion requires T > π/ω; at equality only the stated modal second-variation values are asserted.
The oscillator has m > 0, k > 0 and ω = √(k/m). Dirichlet solutions are restricted to [0,T], whereas initial-value uniqueness is asserted for global solutions on R.

A bounded measure means a finite nonnegative Borel measure whose mass outside some closed ball of positive radius is zero. Integrals are componentwise Lebesgue integrals. The shifted tensor admits zero total mass, and its finiteness is asserted under countable choice.
The parallel-axis identity assumes positive total mass and vanishing first moment. The measure remains fixed while the reference point changes.

The two-mass system assumes m > 0, k ≥ 0 and c ≥ 0. The plus label denotes the in-phase mode with squared frequency k/m; the minus label denotes the anti-phase mode with squared frequency (k+2c)/m. Zero-frequency components are affine. Global growth refers to the unique global extension.
The pendulum estimate uses the Euclidean state norm, its induced operator norm, L = max(1,ω²), positive initial norm δ, and the strict condition δ exp(LT) < r. Its conclusion is restricted to [0,T].
All verification items concern mathematical models and exact expressions; they assert no measured parameters, physical applicability or empirical agreement.

load_bearing.statement: For a C² time-dependent Lagrangian chart, a C² admissible curve q and a fixed-endpoint C² variation η, the family ε ↦ S(q+εη) is C² on a sufficiently small open interval, its second derivative is the integral of the displayed Hessian quadratic form H(ε,t), and δ²S(q)[η,η] = ∫ H(0,t) dt.

For g,l > 0, ω² = g/l, F(θ,v) = (v,−ω² sin θ), A = DF(0), and L = max(1,ω²), F is globally L-Lipschitz, ||A|| = L, and on ||z|| ≤ r its remainder is bounded by (ω²r/6)||z||². If δ = ||z₀|| > 0 and δ exp(LT) < r, the maximal nonlinear solution exists on [0,T] and differs from the linear solution with the same datum by at most (ω²r/6)δ²∫₀ᵗ exp(||A||(t−s))exp(2Ls) ds, hence by (ω²r/6)δ²t exp((||A||+2L)t).

For m > 0, k,c ≥ 0 and K with rows (k+c,−c), (−c,k+c), the orthonormal vectors u± = (1,±1)/√2 have eigenvalues k and k+2c. The equation mx″ = −Kx is bijectively equivalent to my+″+ky+ = 0 and my−″+(k+2c)y− = 0. For k > 0 its complete solution family has frequencies √(k/m), √((k+2c)/m); for k = 0 the plus component is affine, and the minus component is oscillatory when c > 0 and affine when c = 0.

Assume countable choice. For a finite Borel measure ν with ν(R³ outside the closed ball of radius R) = 0, R > 0, and a ∈ R³, every shifted inertia integrand is Borel measurable and ν-integrable, and |Iν(a)jk| ≤ 2(R+||a||₂)²ν(R³).
Assume countable choice. For a centred mass distribution ν on R³ with total mass m ∈ (0,+∞), every a ∈ R³ satisfies Iν(a) = I(ν) + m(||a||₂²I₃ − aaᵀ).

For ω,T > 0 and L(q,v) = (v²−ω²q²)/2, q₀ = 0 is stationary, ηn(t) = sin(nπt/T) has second variation T((nπ/T)²−ω²)/2, and S(εηn) = ε²δ²S(q₀)[ηn,ηn]/2. For T > π/ω arbitrarily C²-small variations have action of either sign. At T = π/ω the n = 1 value is zero and every n ≥ 2 value is positive.

For m,k,T > 0 and ω = √(k/m), xA(t) = A sin(ωt) solves mx″+kx = 0 and has zero final endpoint exactly when A = 0 or ωT ∈ πZ. At T = nπ/ω, n ≥ 1, the zero-endpoint solution space is exactly {xA:A ∈ R}, whereas every initial datum has a unique global solution. These Dirichlet solutions are exactly the stationary zero-endpoint curves for L(q,v) = (v²−ω²q²)/2.

concerns.concern: The Statement defines H using a sum over j,k = 1,…,n and components ηj,ηk. The cited Euclidean and multivariable definitions use coordinates 0,…,n−1; no general one-based relabeling is stated here or on cm-math-variations. In particular, at n = 1 the displayed η1 is outside the native component domain. The intended Hessian formula is correct after an explicit relabeling or index correction. The earlier rigid page supplies a one-based bridge only for dimension three.

F1 writes 'K12 = K21 = −c' and '⟨u,v⟩ = u1v1+u2v2', citing definitions that explicitly index a two-dimensional vector and matrix by 0,1. No two-dimensional one-based bridge is declared. The computations are correct with the intended first/second-component labeling, but that labeling should be defined.

Clause 3 and the proof use y = (y1,y2), z1 and unit vectors e1,e2 while the cited Euclidean supplier uses indices 0,1 in dimension two. An explicit first/second-component relabeling is missing. The intended component estimate and operator-norm calculation are sound.

L2 invokes 'the fundamental theorem' to evaluate an exponential integral, and step 2.1 relies on it, but deps contains neither thm-ftc-second-part nor an equivalent primitive-evaluation supplier. The elementary evaluation is correct; the actual FTC prerequisite should be declared.

alerts.finding: F5 cites thm-cm-homogeneous-oscillator-solution-classification for the assertion that scalar equations have 'the affine family for λi = 0'. That supplier's Statement assumes k > 0 and does not cover zero stiffness. The affine conclusion is true and also supported by the separately cited free-mode theory, but this particular supplier attribution overstates its domain; prop-cm-oscillator-degenerate-and-repulsive-cases supplies the zero-stiffness classification.

seams_checked.note: The undamped classification uses positive stiffness and arbitrary nondegenerate solution intervals; zero stiffness is taken from the separate degenerate proposition. The pendulum specialization preserves every hypothesis of the finite-time linearization theorem, including δ > 0 and δ exp(LT) < r.

The shifted tensor retains finite bounded Borel measures and countable choice. The parallel-axis theorem retains positive total mass and centredness; it does not apply the centred formula to general first moments. The earlier rigid-page prose explicitly defines the three-dimensional one-based notation.

The second-variation definition retains the open C² chart and extension-based C² fixed-endpoint curve convention. The admissibility and stationarity suppliers are used at their stated regularity. The coordinate-label presentation concern is recorded separately.

The oscillator examples use the stated quadratic chart, admissible smooth curves and fixed endpoints. Stationarity is kept separate from extremality, and the common action calculation at T = π is exact.
The two-point measure has positive total mass 2m, bounded support and zero first moment. Its e3 notation agrees with the one-based bridge on the rigid supplier page.

The modal example separates positive and zero stiffness. The pendulum example uses positive initial norm, verifies strict smallness and evaluates the integral bound as a bound rather than identifying it with the actual nonlinear error.
rem-cm04-linear-model-scope cites the pendulum proposition only for finite-time approximation under its explicit small-amplitude and time hypotheses and denies a uniform-in-time conclusion.

ex-cm04-pendulum-small-angle-check explicitly adopts the angular model and normalizes time by one second and velocity as dθ/ds. Its numerical instance preserves δ = 1/100, r = 1/2, T = 1 and the smallness condition, and uses the valid weaker product bound.

The page preserves the distinction between stationarity and minimization and describes the long-interval oscillator check consistently with the saddle supplier. No item on this A page directly invokes a batch-12 result; the requirement provides contextual access.

The two-mass example rescales Euclidean modal vectors by 1/√m for mass normalization and preserves both frequencies and the affine zero mode. The triatomic consistency check uses the allowed c = 0 specialization. Its separate zero-stiffness attribution to another supplier is routed as an alert.

The physical inertia definition uses I(t,p) = R Iν(Rᵀ(p−c)) Rᵀ with centred positive-mass model data and countable choice. The principal-axis proof uses shifted-integrand finiteness without adding atomlessness or nondegeneracy assumptions.

The triangle shift example retains centredness, total mass 3m0 and the inherited countable-choice assumption, then correctly conjugates the reference parallel-axis identity into spatial coordinates. Its direct finite-sum computation agrees with the supplier specialization.
